newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN MUNICH STAY ATOP BUNDESLIGA WITH WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN MUNICH STAY ATOP BUNDESLIGA WITH WIN.

text.p: Bayern Munich stayed atop the German Bundesliga on Saturday with a difficult 1-0 win over Arminia Bielefeld but titleholders Borussia Dortmund remained in hot pursuit with an equally hard-fought 1-0 victory over Rostock.

Tuning up for their UEFA Cup match on Tuesday against FC Valencia, Bayern struggled at home against a tightly packed Bielefeld defence before national mid-fielder Christian Ziege blasted home a 16-metre shot in the 59th minute.
Playing before 55,000 spectators at Munich's Olympia Stadium, Bayern kept the pressure on newly promoted Bielefeld but were unable to penetrate the visitors' various layers of defence.
Bielefeld defender Peter Hobday in particular stood out, completely shutting down Bayern striker Juergen Klinsmann.
"They have every man and mouse available back there," said Bayern President Franz Beckenbauer at halftime. "We have to be patient and try to work the ball more out to the side."
It took another 15 minutes into the second half before Ziege, who had scored the first goal in Germany's 2-0 friendly victory over Poland last week, drilled in the ball from the right side.
Bayern lead the Bundesliga after five matches with 13 points from four wins and a draw. Dortmund are just a point behind with four straight wins after their season-opening loss.
Dortmund, aiming for a third straight league title, scored their first win ever in Rostock with a goal in the game's final minute. Dortmund had lost three previous matches in the Baltic port.
Brasilian Julio Cesar scored in the 90th minute, but Rostock players erupted in protest at the goal, claiming striker Heiko Herrlich had fouled goalie Perry Braeutigam immediately before the score.

Bayer Leverkusen moved up to fourth place with a convincing 3-0 win over 1860 Munich. Former national striker Ulf Kirsten scored twice, which put him atop the league's goalscoring list with six goals in four games this season.
Kirsten, who struggled with just eight goals all last year, had erupted for three goals in Leverkusen's last Bundesliga match against Duisburg two weeks ago.
"I just was trying to make my contribution," Kirsten said. "I'm feeling very fit."

Werder Bremen also moved up with a 3-0 win over St Pauli. They were led by Austrian national striker Andreas Herzog who opened the flood with a goal in the 26th minute and set up several subsequent scoring chances.
"I think this win today shows that we can play with any team at the top of the league," Herzog said.
In other matches, Bochum beat Karlsruhe 3-1 and Schalke stopped Duisburg 1-0. On Friday night, Borussia Moenchengladbach beat Hamburg 3-0 and Fortuna Duesseldorf defeated Freiburg 2-1.
